source.text: תֶּאְשַׁם֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י מָרְתָ֖ה בֵּֽאלֹהֶ֑יהָ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֔לוּ עֹלְלֵיהֶ֣ם יְרֻטָּ֔שׁוּ וְהָרִיּוֹתָ֖יו יְבֻקָּֽעוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Samaria will bear guilt, for she has rebelled against her God; by the sword they will fall; their infants will be dashed to pieces, and its pregnant [women] will be ripped open.

en.L: Samaria will be held guilty, \q for she has rebelled against her God; \q by the sword they will fall; \q their little ones will be dashed to pieces, \q and her pregnant women ripped open.
en.B: Samaria must bear her guilt, \q because she rebelled against her God. \q By the sword they will fall; \q their little children will be dashed to pieces, \q her pregnant women ripped open.
en.R: The people of Samaria must pay for their guilt, \q because they turned against their God. \q They will be killed in war. \q Their children will be smashed to death, \q and their pregnant women will be cut open.

es.L: Samaria será tenida por culpable, \q porque se rebeló contra su Dios; \q a espada caerán; \q sus pequeños serán estrellados, \q y sus mujeres encintas, abiertas en canal.
es.B: Samaria tendrá que cargar con su culpa, \q porque se rebeló contra su Dios. \q Caerán a espada; \q sus niños serán estrellados, \q y sus mujeres embarazadas, abiertas en canal.
es.R: La gente de Samaria tendrá que pagar por su culpa, \q porque se puso en contra de su Dios. \q Morirán en la guerra. \q Sus niños serán aplastados hasta morir, \q y a sus mujeres embarazadas las abrirán con la espada.

ko.L: 사마리아가 죄의 벌을 받을 것이다. \q 사마리아가 자기 하나님을 거역했기 때문이다. \q 그들은 칼에 쓰러지고, \q 그들의 어린아이들은 박살이 나고, \q 그 임신한 여자들은 배가 갈라질 것이다.
ko.B: 사마리아는 자기 죄의 값을 치러야 한다. \q 자기 하나님께 반역했기 때문이다. \q 그들은 칼에 쓰러질 것이다. \q 그들의 어린아이들은 박살이 나고, \q 임신한 여자들은 배가 갈라질 것이다.
ko.R: 사마리아 백성은 자기 죄의 값을 치러야 한다. \q 그들이 자기 하나님께 등을 돌렸기 때문이다. \q 그들은 전쟁에서 죽을 것이다. \q 그들의 아이들은 내던져져 죽고, \q 임신한 여자들은 배가 갈라질 것이다.

fr.L: Samarie sera tenue pour coupable, \q car elle s’est révoltée contre son Dieu ; \q par l’épée ils tomberont ; \q leurs petits enfants seront écrasés, \q et ses femmes enceintes éventrées.
fr.B: Samarie doit porter sa culpabilité, \q parce qu’elle s’est révoltée contre son Dieu. \q Ils tomberont par l’épée ; \q leurs petits enfants seront écrasés, \q ses femmes enceintes éventrées.
fr.R: Les habitants de Samarie doivent payer pour leur culpabilité, \q parce qu’ils se sont tournés contre leur Dieu. \q Ils seront tués à la guerre. \q Leurs enfants seront écrasés à mort, \q et leurs femmes enceintes seront éventrées.

decisions.choice: This verse is 14:1 in the Hebrew text, 13:16 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 14 with this verse, which closes the judgment of chapter 13. Many Bibles number it 13:16, so their 14:1-9 is 14:2-10 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Hosea is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital of the northern kingdom, and the cruelty of ancient war
decisions.reason: Samaria fell to Assyria in 722 BC after a siege of three years (2 Kings 17:5-6). Killing children and pregnant women was a known horror of war in that time (2 Kings 8:12; 15:16; Amos 1:13), and Hosea has already spoken of it in 10:14. The verse says what will happen; it does not approve it.

decisions.choice: will bear her guilt: be held guilty and suffer its penalty
alternatives: will be made desolate (a closely related verb, as some ancient versions take it)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be guilty and so to bear the punishment of guilt (10:2; 13:1, "he became guilty"). Some ancient versions translate it as "be destroyed" or "be desolate", from a verb that sounds similar.

decisions.choice: The people of Samaria ... they; killed in war
alternatives: Samaria ... she; fall by the sword
decisions.reason: Readable names the city's people, who are meant, and says what falling by the sword means. Literal and Balanced keep the city as "she".

decisions.choice: Hebrew verse numbers are kept (14:1–10); Samaria is repeated rather than called "그녀"
decisions.reason: Korean Bibles number this verse 13:16 and the rest of the chapter one lower, as the shared footnote says. A city pictured as a woman is named again rather than given the written pronoun, as in the published prophets.

decisions.choice: feminine agreement for Samaria ("elle s'est révoltée")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the city as a woman, as the term sheet sets for Samaria; Readable speaks of its people, as the English Readable does.

source.text: שׁ֚וּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֥י כָשַׁ֖לְתָּ בַּעֲוֺנֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Return, O Israel, to Yahweh your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity.

en.L: Return, O Israel, all the way to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q for you have stumbled through your iniquity.
en.B: Return, Israel, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q for your guilt has made you stumble.
en.R: People of Israel, come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. \q Your sins have made you fall.

es.L: Vuelve, oh Israel, hasta {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, \q porque has tropezado por tu iniquidad.
es.B: Vuelve, Israel, {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios, \q porque tu culpa te ha hecho tropezar.
es.R: Pueblo de Israel, vuelve {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios. \q Tus pecados te han hecho caer.

ko.L: 이스라엘아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 네 하나님께로 끝까지 돌아오너라. \q 네가 네 죄악 때문에 넘어졌다.
ko.B: 이스라엘아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 네 하나님께 돌아오너라. \q 너는 네 죄 때문에 넘어졌다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성아, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 너희 하나님께 돌아오너라. \q 너희는 너희 죄 때문에 넘어졌다.

fr.L: Reviens, ô Israël, jusqu’{{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ton Dieu, \q car tu as trébuché par ton iniquité.
fr.B: Reviens, Israël, {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ton Dieu, \q car ta faute t’a fait trébucher.
fr.R: Peuple d’Israël, reviens {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ton Dieu. \q Tes péchés t’ont fait tomber.

decisions.choice: This verse is 14:2 in the Hebrew text, 14:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text chapter 14 begins with the verse about Samaria (14:1), which many Bibles number 13:16. So 14:2-10 here are 14:1-9 there. Hosea is cited by the Hebrew numbers throughout.

decisions.choice: return all the way to: turn back to God completely
decisions.reason: The preposition means "as far as", "right up to" (Joel 2:12; Amos 4:6-11). The verb "return" is the key word of this last section: the people return (14:2-3), God heals their "turning away" (14:5), and his anger "turns" from them (14:5).

decisions.choice: you have stumbled: the word that runs through the book to its last verse
decisions.reason: Hosea has said that priest and prophet stumble (4:5) and that Israel and Ephraim stumble in their guilt (5:5). The book ends with the same word: rebels stumble in the ways of the LORD (14:10).

decisions.choice: People of Israel, come back; fall
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the people, uses the everyday "come back", and says "fall", which keeps the picture of tripping on the way.

decisions.choice: "Vuelve" (tú)
decisions.reason: Israel is addressed as one person here, as the Hebrew has it; shuv of turning back to God is "volver", never "arrepentirse".

decisions.choice: "돌아오너라" for *shuv*
decisions.reason: "Return" is 돌아오다 at every level in the prophets, keeping 회개하다 for the New Testament's Greek.

source.text: קְח֤וּ עִמָּכֶם֙ דְּבָרִ֔ים וְשׁ֖וּבוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה אִמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כָּל־תִּשָּׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְקַח־ט֔וֹב וּֽנְשַׁלְּמָ֥ה פָרִ֖ים שְׂפָתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Take with you words and return to Yahweh; say to him, all you will forgive iniquity, and take good, and we will pay bulls of our lips.

en.L: Take words with you \q and return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Take away all iniquity, and accept [what is] good, \q and we will pay [as] bulls our lips.
en.B: Take words with you \q and return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Take away all guilt, and accept what is good, \q and we will offer our lips in place of bulls.
en.R: Bring your words of repentance with you \q and come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Forgive all our sins and accept what is good. \q Instead of bulls, we will offer {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the words of our lips.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} palabras con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} \q y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}; \q {{plural_you:díganle|decidle}}: «Quita toda iniquidad, y acepta [lo] bueno, \q y pagaremos [como] toros [la ofrenda de] nuestros labios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Lleven|Llevad}} palabras con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} \q y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}}: «Quita toda culpa y acepta lo que es bueno, \q y en lugar de toros {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ofreceremos nuestros labios.
es.R: {{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} palabras de arrepentimiento \q y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q {{plural_you:Díganle|Decidle}}: «Perdona todos nuestros pecados y acepta lo que es bueno. \q En lugar de toros, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ofreceremos las palabras de nuestros labios.

ko.L: 너희는 말을 가지고 \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로 돌아와서 \q 그분께 말하여라. "모든 죄악을 없애 주시고, 좋은 것을 받아 주십시오. \q 저희가 수소 [대신에] 저희 입술을 바치겠습니다.
ko.B: 너희는 드릴 말씀을 준비하여 \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 돌아와서 \q 그분께 아뢰어라. "저희의 모든 죄를 없애 주시고, 좋은 것을 받아 주십시오. \q 저희가 수소 대신에 저희 입술의 고백을 바치겠습니다.
ko.R: 회개하는 말을 가지고 \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 돌아와서 \q 그분께 이렇게 말씀드려라. "저희의 모든 죄를 용서해 주시고 좋은 것을 받아 주십시오. \q 수소 대신에 저희 입술의 말을 주님께 드리겠습니다.

fr.L: Prenez avec vous des paroles \q et revenez {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ; \q dites-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Ôte toute iniquité, et accepte [ce qui est] bon, \q et nous paierons [comme] taureaux nos lèvres.
fr.B: Prenez avec vous des paroles \q et revenez {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q Dites-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Enlève toute faute, et accepte ce qui est bon, \q et nous offrirons nos lèvres à la place des taureaux.
fr.R: Apportez avec vous des paroles pour demander pardon \q et revenez {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q Dites-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : « Pardonne tous nos péchés et accepte ce qui est bon. \q Au lieu de taureaux, nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} offrirons les paroles de nos lèvres.

decisions.choice: take words with you: come with a spoken confession and prayer
decisions.reason: Worshipers brought gifts and animals when they came before God (Exodus 23:15). Hosea tells Israel to bring words instead, and gives them the words to say. Earlier the people's sacrifices without loyalty were refused (6:6; 8:13).

decisions.choice: take away all iniquity, and accept what is good: a plea for forgiveness and for God to receive the people's offering
alternatives: "accept good [words]", that is, the confession they bring
decisions.reason: The Hebrew order is unusual, with "all" first and the verb in the middle, but the sense is clear: "forgive all iniquity". "Accept what is good" most likely asks God to receive what they now bring, their words of return.

decisions.choice: bulls of our lips: words of prayer and praise offered in place of bulls
alternatives: "the fruit of our lips" (the Septuagint, reading the same letters as "fruit" with an added ending)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "bulls". If the letters are divided differently, the word becomes "fruit", and the Septuagint reads "the fruit of our lips". Either way the offering is made with the lips. The verb "pay" is used of paying vows and offerings to God (Psalm 50:14; 116:14), and Psalm 51:17-19 and 69:31-32 also prefer words of praise and a humble heart to bulls. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: Hebrews 13:15 follows the Greek: "a sacrifice of praise ... the fruit of lips"
decisions.reason: Hebrews 13:15 calls believers to offer God "a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name". It uses the Greek wording of this verse (m3).

decisions.choice: we will offer our lips in place of bulls (B); Instead of bulls, we will offer you the words of our lips (R)
alternatives: we will pay the bulls of our lips
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the bare phrase. Balanced and Readable say what it means (m3): the lips, and the words they speak, are the offering, in place of animals.

decisions.choice: words of repentance; our sins
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of words they bring, which the prayer that follows makes plain, and whose sins are meant. The prayer continues in 14:4, so the quotation is closed there.

decisions.choice: "[[Tomen|Tomad]]", "[[díganle|decidle]]"; the people's prayer in « » running into 14:4
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, addressed to the people, so they take the plural_you span; the prayer the people are to say takes quotation marks and closes at the end of verse 4, as in the English. In the prayer God is addressed as tú.

decisions.choice: "pagaremos [como] toros [la ofrenda de] nuestros labios"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "bulls of our lips" cannot stand word for word in Spanish; Literal brackets the words it needs.

decisions.choice: The people's prayer (14:3–4) is in 합쇼체 with "저희"
decisions.reason: Communal prayer to God takes 합쇼체 with "저희", as in the prophets' prayers. Hebrews 13:15 ("입술의 열매") follows the Greek; Korean keeps the Hebrew "bulls of our lips" as an offering of words.

decisions.choice: "vous" to the people, the prayer they are given in « » from here to the end of verse 4, with "tu" and deity_pronoun spans for God inside it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the people in the plural and gives them the words to say; the quoted prayer is speech inside the oracle and takes French quotation marks, as the English has them.

source.text: אַשּׁ֣וּר׀לֹ֣א יוֹשִׁיעֵ֗נוּ עַל־סוּס֙ לֹ֣א נִרְכָּ֔ב וְלֹא־נֹ֥אמַר ע֛וֹד אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁר־בְּךָ֖ יְרֻחַ֥ם יָתֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Assyria will not save us; on horse[s] we will not ride, and we will not say again, our God, to [the] work of our hands, for in you is shown compassion [the] fatherless.

en.L: Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses, \q and we will not say again, 'Our god,' to the work of our hands; \q for in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the fatherless finds compassion."
en.B: Assyria cannot save us; we will not ride on horses. \q Never again will we say 'Our god' to what our own hands have made, \q for in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the orphan finds compassion."
en.R: Assyria cannot save us, and we will not trust in war horses. \q We will never again call the idols we have made 'our god.' \q You are the one who shows mercy to children who have no father."

es.L: Asiria no nos salvará; no montaremos a caballo, \q y no diremos más: “Dios nuestro”, a la obra de nuestras manos; \q porque en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} el huérfano halla compasión».
es.B: Asiria no puede salvarnos; no montaremos a caballo. \q Nunca más diremos “Dios nuestro” a lo que han hecho nuestras manos, \q porque en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} el huérfano halla compasión».
es.R: Asiria no puede salvarnos, y no confiaremos en caballos de guerra. \q Nunca más llamaremos “nuestro dios” a los ídolos que hemos hecho. \q Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quien muestra compasión a los niños que no tienen padre».

ko.L: 앗시리아가 저희를 구원하지 못할 것입니다. 저희가 말을 타지 않겠습니다. \q 저희 손으로 만든 것에게 다시는 '우리 신'이라고 말하지 않겠습니다. \q 고아가 주님께 긍휼을 입기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 앗시리아는 저희를 구원할 수 없습니다. 저희는 말을 타지 않겠습니다. \q 저희 손으로 만든 것을 보고 다시는 '우리 신'이라고 부르지 않겠습니다. \q 고아가 주님께 긍휼을 입습니다."
ko.R: 앗시리아는 저희를 구할 수 없습니다. 저희는 전쟁에 쓰는 말을 믿지 않겠습니다. \q 저희가 만든 우상들을 다시는 '우리 신'이라고 부르지 않겠습니다. \q 아버지 없는 아이들을 불쌍히 여기시는 분은 주님이십니다."

fr.L: L’Assyrie ne nous sauvera pas ; nous ne monterons pas sur des chevaux, \q et nous ne dirons plus : “Notre dieu” à l’ouvrage de nos mains ; \q car c’est auprès de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que l’orphelin trouve compassion. »
fr.B: L’Assyrie ne peut pas nous sauver ; nous ne monterons pas sur des chevaux. \q Jamais plus nous ne dirons “Notre dieu” à ce que nos mains ont fabriqué, \q car c’est auprès de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que l’orphelin trouve compassion. »
fr.R: L’Assyrie ne peut pas nous sauver, et nous ne compterons pas sur des chevaux de guerre. \q Nous n’appellerons plus jamais “notre dieu” les idoles que nous avons fabriquées. \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui as pitié des enfants qui n’ont pas de père. »

decisions.choice: Assyria and horses: the help Israel looked for from the great powers
decisions.reason: Israel had turned to Assyria for help (5:13; 7:11; 8:9; 12:2). Horses mean chariot forces, which Israel looked for from Egypt (Isaiah 31:1; Deuteronomy 17:16). In this prayer the people give up both kinds of help.

decisions.choice: "Our god" to the work of our hands: calling idols god
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for God is a plural form that can also mean "gods". Here it is what the people called their images, which are "the work of our hands" (13:2; 8:6).

decisions.choice: finds compassion: the word of the name "No Compassion" (1:6)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the name of Hosea's daughter, whose name said that God would no longer show compassion to Israel (1:6), and in the promise of 2:25 that he will. The fatherless are the most helpless people, whom God protects (Deuteronomy 10:18; Psalm 68:6). The people admit that they are as helpless as orphans.

decisions.choice: trust in war horses; the idols we have made
alternatives: ride on horses; the work of our hands
decisions.reason: Readable says what riding on horses stands for (m1) and what "the work of our hands" means (m2). It turns the last clause into a direct statement to God.

decisions.choice: “ ” inside « »
decisions.reason: Words quoted inside the people's prayer take the inner Spanish quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "halla compasión" (L, B); "muestra compasión" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in the name "No Compadecida" (1:6), so Spanish keeps "compasión" to let the echo be heard.

decisions.choice: "긍휼을 입다" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The verb of the name "긍휼 없음" (1:6), so the reversal at the book's end can be heard.

source.text: אֶרְפָּא֙ מְשׁ֣וּבָתָ֔ם אֹהֲבֵ֖ם נְדָבָ֑ה כִּ֛י שָׁ֥ב אַפִּ֖י מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I will heal their turning away; I will love them freely, for has turned my anger from him.

en.L: I will heal their turning away; \q I will love them freely, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger has turned from him.
en.B: I will heal their unfaithfulness; \q I will love them freely, \q for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger has turned away from them.
en.R: I will heal them of turning away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I will love them freely, \q because I am no longer angry with them.

es.L: Sanaré su apostasía; \q los amaré de pura gracia, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira se ha apartado de él.
es.B: Sanaré su infidelidad; \q los amaré generosamente, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira se ha apartado de ellos.
es.R: Los sanaré de su costumbre de alejarse de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Los amaré generosamente, \q porque ya no estoy enojado con ellos.

ko.L: 내가 그들의 배반을 고치고, \q 기꺼이 그들을 사랑하겠다. \q 내 분노가 그에게서 떠났기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들의 배신하는 병을 고쳐 주고, \q 아낌없이 그들을 사랑하겠다. \q 내 분노가 그들에게서 떠났다.
ko.R: 나는 그들이 나에게서 떠나가는 병을 고쳐 주겠다. \q 아낌없이 그들을 사랑하겠다. \q 나는 더 이상 그들에게 화가 나 있지 않다.

fr.L: Je guérirai leur infidélité ; \q je les aimerai de bon cœur, \q car {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère s’est détournée de lui.
fr.B: Je guérirai leur infidélité ; \q je les aimerai de bon cœur, \q car {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère s’est détournée d’eux.
fr.R: Je les guérirai de leur habitude de se détourner de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Je les aimerai de bon cœur, \q parce que je ne suis plus en colère contre eux.

decisions.choice: God answers: the speaker changes from the people's prayer to God
decisions.reason: After the prayer of 14:3-4, God speaks in the first person to the end of 14:9. His answer gives the people more than they asked: healing, love and life.

decisions.choice: their turning away: their unfaithfulness to God, which God will heal like a disease
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "return", which runs through 14:2-5. Israel was "bent on turning away" (11:7); now God will heal it, as Jeremiah 3:22 also promises. In the same verse God's anger "has turned", from the same verb.

decisions.choice: freely: of my own will, as a gift that is not earned or forced
decisions.reason: The word is used for a freewill offering, a gift brought because the giver wants to (Exodus 35:29; Psalm 54:8).

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew changes from "them" to "him", meaning Israel as one people. Balanced and Readable keep "them" so the change does not confuse; Literal keeps "him". Balanced says "unfaithfulness" for "turning away" (m2).

source.text: אֶהְיֶ֤ה כַטַּל֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִפְרַ֖ח כַּשּֽׁוֹשַׁנָּ֑ה וְיַ֥ךְ שָׁרָשָׁ֖יו כַּלְּבָנֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily, and he will strike his roots like Lebanon.

en.L: I will be like the dew to Israel; \q he will bloom like the lily, \q and he will strike his roots like Lebanon.
en.B: To Israel I will be like the dew; \q he will blossom like a lily \q and send down his roots like the cedars of Lebanon.
en.R: I will be like dew for Israel. \q Israel will bloom like a lily, \q and its roots will go deep like the cedars of Lebanon.

es.L: Seré como el rocío para Israel; \q florecerá como el lirio, \q y echará sus raíces como el Líbano.
es.B: Para Israel seré como el rocío; \q florecerá como un lirio \q y echará raíces como los cedros del Líbano.
es.R: Seré como el rocío para Israel. \q Israel florecerá como un lirio, \q y sus raíces se hundirán como las de los cedros del Líbano.

ko.L: 내가 이스라엘에게 이슬 같을 것이니, \q 그가 백합화처럼 피고, \q 레바논처럼 뿌리를 내릴 것이다.
ko.B: 나는 이스라엘에게 이슬처럼 되겠다. \q 그는 백합꽃처럼 피어나고, \q 레바논의 백향목처럼 뿌리를 깊이 내릴 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 이스라엘에게 이슬처럼 되겠다. \q 이스라엘은 백합꽃처럼 피어날 것이다. \q 레바논의 백향목처럼 뿌리를 깊이 내릴 것이다.

fr.L: Je serai comme la rosée pour Israël ; \q il fleurira comme le lis, \q et il enfoncera ses racines comme le Liban.
fr.B: Pour Israël je serai comme la rosée ; \q il fleurira comme un lis \q et enfoncera ses racines comme les cèdres du Liban.
fr.R: Je serai comme la rosée pour Israël. \q Israël fleurira comme un lis, \q et ses racines iront profond comme celles des cèdres du Liban.

decisions.choice: like the dew: the picture of 6:4 and 13:3 turned around
decisions.reason: In 6:4 and 13:3 dew is something that is gone by mid-morning. Here God himself is the dew. In a land with no rain for months in summer, dew keeps plants alive, and it is a sign of blessing (Genesis 27:28; Deuteronomy 33:28).

decisions.choice: strike his roots like Lebanon: roots as deep and strong as the great trees of Lebanon
decisions.reason: Lebanon was known for its forests of cedar (Psalm 104:16; Isaiah 2:13). The lily blooms quickly; the cedar stands for strength and permanence. Lebanon is named three times in 14:6-8.

decisions.choice: the cedars of Lebanon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the trees that the comparison means (m2); Literal keeps "Lebanon". Readable says "its roots" because it names Israel instead of using "he".

source.text: יֵֽלְכוּ֙ יֹֽנְקוֹתָ֔יו וִיהִ֥י כַזַּ֖יִת הוֹד֑וֹ וְרֵ֥יחַֽ ל֖וֹ כַּלְּבָנֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Will go out his shoots, and will be like the olive tree his splendor, and his fragrance like Lebanon.

en.L: His young shoots will spread out, \q and his splendor will be like the olive tree, \q and his fragrance like Lebanon.
en.B: His young shoots will spread out; \q his beauty will be like the olive tree's, \q his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon.
en.R: Israel will spread out new branches. \q It will be beautiful like an olive tree \q and smell sweet like the cedars of Lebanon.

es.L: Se extenderán sus renuevos, \q y será su esplendor como el del olivo, \q y su fragancia como el Líbano.
es.B: Sus renuevos se extenderán; \q su belleza será como la del olivo, \q su fragancia como la de los cedros del Líbano.
es.R: Israel extenderá ramas nuevas. \q Será hermoso como un olivo \q y tendrá un olor agradable como los cedros del Líbano.

ko.L: 그의 어린 가지들이 뻗어 나가고, \q 그의 아름다움은 올리브나무 같고, \q 그의 향기는 레바논 같을 것이다.
ko.B: 그의 어린 가지들이 뻗어 나가고, \q 그 아름다움은 올리브나무 같고, \q 그 향기는 레바논의 백향목 같을 것이다.
ko.R: 이스라엘은 새 가지를 뻗을 것이다. \q 올리브나무처럼 아름답고, \q 레바논의 백향목처럼 향기로울 것이다.

fr.L: Ses jeunes pousses s’étendront, \q et sa splendeur sera comme l’olivier, \q et son parfum comme le Liban.
fr.B: Ses jeunes pousses s’étendront ; \q sa beauté sera celle de l’olivier, \q son parfum celui des cèdres du Liban.
fr.R: Israël étendra de nouvelles branches. \q Il sera beau comme un olivier \q et sentira bon comme les cèdres du Liban.

decisions.choice: the olive tree: green all year, long-lived and fruitful
decisions.reason: The olive tree keeps its leaves and lives for centuries, and its oil was one of the land's chief riches. It is a picture of a people blessed by God in Psalm 52:10 and Jeremiah 11:16.

decisions.choice: his fragrance like Lebanon: the scent of its cedar forests, as in the Song of Songs
decisions.reason: Song of Songs 4:11 speaks of "the fragrance of Lebanon". Cedar wood is fragrant. The pictures of 14:6-8 (lily, Lebanon, vine, wine, shade) are also those of the Song's garden of love.

decisions.choice: the cedars of Lebanon
decisions.reason: As in 14:6, Balanced and Readable name the trees that give Lebanon its scent (m2). Readable names Israel and says "smell sweet" for "fragrance".

source.text: יָשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בְצִלּ֔וֹ יְחַיּ֥וּ דָגָ֖ן וְיִפְרְח֣וּ כַגָּ֑פֶן זִכְר֖וֹ כְּיֵ֥ין לְבָנֽוֹן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They will return, those dwelling in his shade; they will revive [like] grain, and they will blossom like the vine; his remembrance [will be] like the wine of Lebanon.

en.L: Those who dwell in his shade will return; \q they will revive [like] grain, and they will blossom like the vine; \q his renown [will be] as the wine of Lebanon.
en.B: Those who live in his shade will come back; \q they will flourish like grain and blossom like the vine; \q his fame will be like the wine of Lebanon.
en.R: People will come back to live in Israel's shade. \q They will grow like grain and bloom like a vine. \q Israel will be famous like the wine of Lebanon.

es.L: Volverán los que habitan a su sombra; \q revivirán [como] el grano, y florecerán como la vid; \q su renombre [será] como el vino del Líbano.
es.B: Los que viven a su sombra volverán; \q crecerán como el grano y florecerán como la vid; \q su fama será como la del vino del Líbano.
es.R: La gente volverá a vivir a la sombra de Israel. \q Crecerán como el grano y florecerán como una vid. \q Israel será famoso como el vino del Líbano.

ko.L: 그의 그늘 아래 사는 자들이 돌아올 것이다. \q 그들은 곡식처럼 다시 살아나고, 포도나무처럼 꽃을 피울 것이다. \q 그의 명성은 레바논의 포도주 같을 것이다.
ko.B: 그의 그늘 아래 사는 사람들이 돌아올 것이다. \q 그들은 곡식처럼 다시 살아나고 포도나무처럼 꽃을 피울 것이다. \q 그의 이름은 레바논의 포도주처럼 널리 알려질 것이다.
ko.R: 사람들이 돌아와 이스라엘의 그늘 아래 살 것이다. \q 그들은 곡식처럼 자라고 포도나무처럼 꽃을 피울 것이다. \q 이스라엘은 레바논의 포도주처럼 이름이 날 것이다.

fr.L: Ceux qui habitent à son ombre reviendront ; \q ils revivront [comme] le blé, et ils fleuriront comme la vigne ; \q sa renommée [sera] comme le vin du Liban.
fr.B: Ceux qui habitent à son ombre reviendront ; \q ils reprendront vie comme le blé et fleuriront comme la vigne ; \q sa renommée sera comme celle du vin du Liban.
fr.R: Les gens reviendront habiter à l’ombre d’Israël. \q Ils pousseront comme le blé et fleuriront comme une vigne. \q Israël sera célèbre comme le vin du Liban.

decisions.choice: those who dwell in his shade: people living under the shelter of Israel, the tree of 14:6-7
alternatives: God's shade (God speaks of himself as a tree in 14:9)
"they will again dwell in his shade" ("return" used as "again")
decisions.reason: "His" most naturally refers to Israel, pictured as a spreading tree in 14:6-7. Some take it as God, whose shade gives shelter (14:9; Psalm 91:1). The verb "return" can also mean "do again", so the line may mean that people will again live in its shade.

decisions.choice: they will revive like grain: spring back to life as grain grows from the ground
decisions.reason: The verb means to come to life or to give life. With "grain" it may compare the people to grain that grows again after sowing, or say that they will raise crops. The first fits the comparisons on either side.

decisions.choice: his remembrance: his renown, the name he will have
decisions.reason: The word means what a person is remembered by, their fame (Psalm 102:13). The wine of Lebanon was known for its quality.

decisions.choice: Israel's shade; Israel will be famous
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel for "his", following m1, and says plainly what "remembrance" means (m3).

source.text: אֶפְרַ֕יִם מַה־לִּ֥י ע֖וֹד לָֽעֲצַבִּ֑ים אֲנִ֧י עָנִ֣יתִי וַאֲשׁוּרֶ֗נּוּ אֲנִי֙ כִּבְר֣וֹשׁ רַֽעֲנָ֔ן מִמֶּ֖נִּי פֶּרְיְךָ֥ נִמְצָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Ephraim, what to me again with idols? I have answered, and I will watch him; I [am] like a luxuriant cypress; from me your fruit is found.

en.L: Ephraim, what [have] I to do anymore with idols? \q I have answered and I will watch over him; I [am] like a luxuriant cypress; \q from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} your fruit is found.
en.B: Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? \q I am the one who answers him and watches over him. I am like a cypress, green and full of leaves; \q your fruit comes from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Ephraim, I want nothing more to do with idols! \q I am the one who answers you and takes care of you. I am like a cypress tree that is always green. \q All your fruit comes from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Efraín, ¿qué [tengo] yo que ver ya con los ídolos? \q Yo he respondido y lo cuidaré; yo [soy] como un ciprés frondoso; \q de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} procede tu fruto.
es.B: Efraín, ¿qué tengo yo que ver todavía con los ídolos? \q Yo soy quien le responde y quien lo cuida. Soy como un ciprés verde y frondoso; \q tu fruto procede de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Efraín, ¡no quiero tener nada más que ver con los ídolos! \q Yo soy quien te responde y te cuida. Soy como un ciprés que siempre está verde. \q Todo tu fruto viene de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

ko.L: 에브라임아, 내가 다시 우상들과 무슨 [상관이] 있느냐? \q 내가 응답하였고 그를 돌보겠다. 나는 무성한 잣나무 같다. \q 네 열매가 나에게서 나온다.
ko.B: 에브라임아, 내가 우상들과 더 무슨 상관이 있겠느냐? \q 그에게 응답하고 그를 돌보는 이는 바로 나다. 나는 잎이 무성한 푸른 잣나무와 같다. \q 네 열매는 나에게서 나온다.
ko.R: 에브라임아, 나는 이제 우상들과 아무 상관이 없다! \q 너에게 대답해 주고 너를 돌보는 이는 바로 나다. 나는 늘 푸른 잣나무와 같다. \q 네 모든 열매는 나에게서 나온다.

fr.L: Éphraïm, qu’ai-je encore à faire avec les idoles ? \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui ai répondu et qui veillerai sur lui ; je [suis] comme un cyprès verdoyant ; \q c’est de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} que vient ton fruit.
fr.B: Éphraïm, qu’ai-je encore à faire avec les idoles ? \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui lui réponds et qui veille sur lui. Je suis comme un cyprès vert et plein de feuilles ; \q ton fruit vient de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Éphraïm, je ne veux plus rien avoir à faire avec les idoles ! \q C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui te réponds et qui prends soin de toi. Je suis comme un cyprès toujours vert. \q Tout ton fruit vient de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

decisions.choice: God speaks: "what have I to do anymore with idols?", meaning that their time is over
alternatives: Ephraim speaks: "Ephraim [will say], 'What have I to do anymore with idols?'"
decisions.reason: God has been speaking since 14:5 and goes on in the first person after this line, so the question is most likely his: the idols no longer stand between him and Ephraim. Some read it as the words of Ephraim, renouncing idols, as in 14:4; the Hebrew does not mark the speech.

decisions.choice: I answer and watch over him: God, not Assyria, cares for Ephraim
decisions.reason: "Answer" is used of God answering prayer, as he answers the prayer of 14:3-4 (compare 2:23-24). "Watch over" is the verb used in 13:7 for the leopard lying in wait; the watcher who threatened now protects. The verb also sounds like the name of Assyria, which Israel has just renounced (14:4).

decisions.choice: I am like a luxuriant cypress; from me your fruit is found: God is the source of Ephraim's life and fruit
decisions.reason: This is a rare picture of God as a tree. The cypress (or juniper) keeps its leaves all year, unlike the trees of the fertility gods, under whose shade Israel had worshiped (4:13). "Your fruit" plays again on the name Ephraim, "fruitful" (13:15): what makes Ephraim fruitful comes from God.

decisions.choice: answers you and takes care of you; a cypress tree that is always green
alternatives: answers him and watches over him; a luxuriant cypress
decisions.reason: Readable keeps God speaking to Ephraim throughout instead of changing to "him", and says what is special about the cypress. It states the first line as an exclamation, which is what the question means (m1).

decisions.choice: "잣나무" for *berosh*
decisions.reason: The Kings word for the tree (1 Kings 5:22 and 6:15 in published Korean); "늘 푸른" at R carries the English "always green".

source.text: מִ֤י חָכָם֙ וְיָ֣בֵֽן אֵ֔לֶּה נָב֖וֹן וְיֵֽדָעֵ֑ם כִּֽי־יְשָׁרִ֞ים דַּרְכֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה וְצַדִּקִים֙ יֵ֣לְכוּ בָ֔ם וּפֹשְׁעִ֖ים יִכָּ֥שְׁלוּ בָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] wise, and let him understand these [things]? Discerning, and let him know them? For upright [are the] ways of Yahweh, and righteous [ones] walk in them, and transgressors stumble in them.

en.L: Who [is] wise, that {{gender:they|he}} may understand these [things]? \q Discerning, that {{gender:they|he}} may know them? \q For the ways of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] upright, and the righteous walk in them, \q but transgressors stumble in them.
en.B: Who is wise enough to understand these things? \q Who is discerning enough to know them? \q For the ways of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are right; the righteous walk in them, \q but rebels stumble in them.
en.R: Anyone who is wise will understand these things. \q Anyone with good sense will know what they mean. \q The ways of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are right. Those who do right will walk in them, \q but those who rebel against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will stumble in them.

es.L: ¿Quién [es] sabio, para que entienda estas [cosas]? \q ¿Prudente, para que las conozca? \q Porque los caminos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [son] rectos, y los justos andarán por ellos, \q pero los transgresores tropezarán en ellos.
es.B: ¿Quién es tan sabio como para entender estas cosas? \q ¿Quién es tan prudente como para conocerlas? \q Porque los caminos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} son rectos; los justos andan por ellos, \q pero los rebeldes tropiezan en ellos.
es.R: Quien sea sabio entenderá estas cosas. \q Quien tenga buen juicio sabrá lo que significan. \q Los caminos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} son rectos. Los que hacen lo correcto andarán por ellos, \q pero los que se rebelan contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tropezarán en ellos.

ko.L: 누가 지혜로우냐? 그는 이 일들을 깨달아라. \q 누가 분별력이 있느냐? 그는 이것들을 알아라. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 길은 곧으니, 의인들은 그 길로 걷지만, \q 반역하는 자들은 그 길에서 넘어질 것이다.
ko.B: 누가 이 일들을 깨달을 만큼 지혜로우냐? \q 누가 이것들을 알 만큼 분별력이 있느냐? \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 길은 올바르니, 의로운 사람들은 그 길로 걷지만, \q 반역하는 자들은 그 길에서 넘어질 것이다.
ko.R: 지혜로운 사람은 이 일들을 깨달을 것이다. \q 분별력 있는 사람은 그 뜻을 알 것이다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 길은 바르다. 바르게 사는 사람들은 그 길로 걸을 것이다. \q 그러나 그분께 죄를 짓는 사람들은 그 길에서 넘어질 것이다.

fr.L: Qui [est] sage, pour qu’il comprenne ces [choses] ? \q Intelligent, pour qu’il les connaisse ? \q Car les voies {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [sont] droites, et les justes y marchent, \q mais les transgresseurs y trébuchent.
fr.B: Qui est assez sage pour comprendre ces choses ? \q Qui est assez intelligent pour les connaître ? \q Car les voies {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sont droites ; les justes y marchent, \q mais les rebelles y trébuchent.
fr.R: Celui qui est sage comprendra ces choses. \q Celui qui a du bon sens saura ce qu’elles veulent dire. \q Les chemins {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sont droits. Ceux qui font le bien y marcheront, \q mais ceux qui pèchent contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} y trébucheront.

decisions.choice: a closing wisdom saying: a word to everyone who reads the book
decisions.reason: The book ends with a saying in the language of the wisdom books: the wise and the discerning, the upright ways, the righteous and the rebels (Proverbs 10:29; Psalm 107:43; compare Jeremiah 9:11). It speaks to later readers and tells them to take Hosea's words to heart.

decisions.choice: who is wise, that he may understand?: an invitation, meaning "let whoever is wise understand"
decisions.reason: The question is not asking for a name. It invites any reader who is wise to understand these things, as in Psalm 107:43.

decisions.choice: walk ... stumble: the same ways are a path for some and a stumbling place for others
decisions.reason: "Stumble" picks up 4:5, 5:5 and 14:2, where Israel stumbled in its guilt. The ways of the LORD do not change; what differs is how people walk in them (Proverbs 4:18-19; 10:29).

decisions.choice: rebels (B); those who rebel against him (R)
decisions.reason: The word means those who rebel and break faith. Balanced says "rebels"; Literal keeps "transgressors". Readable says against whom they rebel, and "those who do right" for the righteous.

decisions.choice: Who is wise enough to ...? (B); Anyone who is wise will ... (R)
alternatives: Whoever is wise, let him understand
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the questions and says them in a natural way that needs no pronoun. Readable states the invitation directly (m2). Literal keeps the pronoun as a reader setting.

decisions.choice: no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs a gender setting for "they / he"; Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ("entienda", "conozca"), so there is no pronoun to set.

decisions.choice: "transgresores" (L); "rebeldes" (B); "los que se rebelan" (R)
decisions.reason: Pasha at the levels the English uses here.

decisions.choice: No gender span: Korean needs no pronoun for "he/they" here
decisions.reason: Korean says "누가 … 지혜로우냐? 그는 …" or leaves the subject unsaid, so the English gender span has no second wording.

decisions.choice: *pasha'*: "반역하는 자들" (L, B), "그분께 죄를 짓는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the verb (반역하다 / 반역하다 / 죄를 짓다).

decisions.choice: no gender span on "qu'il comprenne", where the English Literal has "they / he"
decisions.reason: As the style guide and term sheet ask: French "qui ... il" is already generic, so the gender setting goes on nouns only.

decisions.choice: pasha "les transgresseurs" (L), "les rebelles" (B), "ceux qui pèchent contre lui" (R)
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the verb in the Twelve.
